# Cockpit UI

> Eleven ordinary UI controls as the cockpit of a 1990s giant-robot anime: painted pieces on painted backing sheets, screens drawn live, and anime reactions (sound-effect lettering, impact frames, cut-in panels) when you use them. Each is one plain script that registers a custom element, with its paintings inside it: no dependencies, no build step, no other files to fetch. MIT licensed. The robot, the pilot and the crew are original designs.

Live gallery: https://cockpit-ui.vercel.app
Source: https://github.com/finktheartist/cockpit-ui

## Drop-in controls

Each is one plain script that registers a custom element. Load it with a script tag, not as a module. Do not rewrite or split the file: the paintings are inside it as data. Each file carries a copy of the shared core; the first one loaded sets window.Cockpit and the rest reuse it, so any mix shares one clock.

- [Launch](https://cockpit-ui.vercel.app/launch/launch.js) (hold to confirm, about 1144 KB): A red button under an orange guard. Lift the guard, then hold the button: lamps count up, the screen counts down, speed lines close in. Hold to the end and the robot launches across the whole control. `<cockpit-launch>`: Use <cockpit-launch></cockpit-launch>. Listen for cockpit:launch; read el.state (safe, armed, launched); el.reset() puts the guard back. [Docs](https://github.com/finktheartist/cockpit-ui/blob/main/launch/README.md)
- [Output gain](https://cockpit-ui.vercel.app/dial/dial.js) (slider, about 605 KB): A slider that is a dial beside a screen. Turn it and eleven lamps light round it, the number and the trace on the screen climb, and the copy changes at each level. At 100 the pilot cuts in. `<cockpit-dial>`: Use <cockpit-dial value="20"></cockpit-dial>. Read el.value (0 to 100); it fires input while it turns and change when let go. Works in forms with a name. [Docs](https://github.com/finktheartist/cockpit-ui/blob/main/dial/README.md)
- [Pre-launch check](https://cockpit-ui.vercel.app/checklist/checklist.js) (checkboxes, about 559 KB): Four latching buttons with lit labels and a screen that keeps the tally. Tick all four and the deck crew wave you off. `<cockpit-checklist>`: Use <cockpit-checklist></cockpit-checklist>. Read el.value (four digits such as "1010") and el.complete; it fires input and change. Works in forms with a name. [Docs](https://github.com/finktheartist/cockpit-ui/blob/main/checklist/README.md)
- [Safety lock](https://cockpit-ui.vercel.app/lock/lock.js) (switch, about 757 KB): A heavy toggle between LOCK and RELEASE beside a screen listing four clamps. Throw it and the clamps let go one after another; when the last one goes, the restraints blow off. `<cockpit-lock>`: Use <cockpit-lock></cockpit-lock>. Read el.checked and listen for change. Works in forms with a name. [Docs](https://github.com/finktheartist/cockpit-ui/blob/main/lock/README.md)
- [Drive mode](https://cockpit-ui.vercel.app/mode/mode.js) (radio group, about 529 KB): Four key caps: cruise, combat, snipe, stealth. The chosen one lights in its own colour and the screen redraws for it. Choosing combat brings the robot's fist. `<cockpit-mode>`: Use <cockpit-mode></cockpit-mode>. Read el.value (cruise, combat, snipe or stealth); it fires input and change. Works in forms with a name. [Docs](https://github.com/finktheartist/cockpit-ui/blob/main/mode/README.md)
- [Alert](https://cockpit-ui.vercel.app/alert/alert.js) (notification, about 542 KB): A warning panel: three level lamps, a hazard-striped window and an ACKNOWLEDGE bar. It shows a notice, a caution or a warning; a warning flashes red and brings the missiles. `<cockpit-alert>`: Use <cockpit-alert></cockpit-alert> and call el.show("warning", "Disk almost full"). Listen for cockpit:ack; read el.level. [Docs](https://github.com/finktheartist/cockpit-ui/blob/main/alert/README.md)
- [Monitor select](https://cockpit-ui.vercel.app/tabs/tabs.js) (tabs, about 519 KB): Three key caps over a monitor: main, sub and rear. Changing tab cuts through static. Stay on the rear camera for a moment and a contact turns up. `<cockpit-tabs>`: Use <cockpit-tabs></cockpit-tabs>. Read el.value (main, sub or rear); it fires input and change. [Docs](https://github.com/finktheartist/cockpit-ui/blob/main/tabs/README.md)
- [Agent state](https://cockpit-ui.vercel.app/agent/agent.js) (status display, about 2.8 MB): A status display for an AI agent. The robot stands as a hologram on a projector base and turns; its pose and colour follow the state (standby, thinking, working, waiting, done, error) and a window names the task. `<cockpit-agent>`: Use <cockpit-agent></cockpit-agent> and call el.set("working", "reading 12 files"). States: standby, thinking, working, waiting, done, error. It fires cockpit:state. [Docs](https://github.com/finktheartist/cockpit-ui/blob/main/agent/README.md)
- [System load](https://cockpit-ui.vercel.app/loading/loading.js) (loading bar, about 442 KB): A long gauge with a segmented bar and a number window. Feed it progress and the line under it reports what is starting up; at 100 the robot's visor lights. `<cockpit-loading>`: Use <cockpit-loading></cockpit-loading> and call el.set(0.4) with progress from 0 to 1. Add the demo attribute to make it run by itself. It fires cockpit:done at 100. [Docs](https://github.com/finktheartist/cockpit-ui/blob/main/loading/README.md)
- [Active time](https://cockpit-ui.vercel.app/stepper/stepper.js) (stepper, about 516 KB): Minus and plus keys round an amber window, with a strip of ten lamps. Each press is thirty seconds; hold to repeat. At five minutes the power cable comes out. `<cockpit-stepper>`: Use <cockpit-stepper value="120"></cockpit-stepper>. Read el.value in seconds (30 to 300); it fires input and change. Works in forms with a name. [Docs](https://github.com/finktheartist/cockpit-ui/blob/main/stepper/README.md)
- [Callsign](https://cockpit-ui.vercel.app/input/input.js) (text input, about 480 KB): A real text field in a long green window, with a character count and a small speaker screen. Typing rattles the keys; Enter registers the name and the bridge answers. `<cockpit-input>`: Use <cockpit-input></cockpit-input>. Read el.value; it fires input, change, and cockpit:enter with { value } when Enter is pressed. Works in forms with a name. [Docs](https://github.com/finktheartist/cockpit-ui/blob/main/input/README.md)

Install any one with the shadcn CLI: `npx shadcn add finktheartist/cockpit-ui/NAME`, where NAME is launch, dial, checklist, lock, mode, alert, tabs, agent, loading, stepper, input. The file lands in `public/cockpit-ui/`.

Each is a painting 640 pixels wide at most with real controls over it; in a narrower container it scales. They are drawn for a dark page. Attributes set the starting state; use properties and methods after that. Each says a line about what just happened: el.line, and a cockpit:line event with { text }. Shaking, impact frames and cut-ins are skipped for prefers-reduced-motion.

## The skill

- [cockpit-ui skill](https://cockpit-ui.vercel.app/skills/cockpit-ui/SKILL.md): the workflow and rules these were made by. Install with `npx skills add finktheartist/cockpit-ui`.
- [core.js](https://cockpit-ui.vercel.app/skills/cockpit-ui/core.js): the shared core (the clock, the custom-element base, lettering, impact frames, the cut-in, drawn screens).
- [starter.html](https://cockpit-ui.vercel.app/skills/cockpit-ui/starter.html): the smallest whole example, a mute switch.
- [look.mjs](https://cockpit-ui.vercel.app/skills/cockpit-ui/look.mjs): photographs a page at chosen moments after an action and saves the frames side by side.

## How the art was made

- [making-of/README.md](https://cockpit-ui.vercel.app/making-of/README.md): how the look was found, how the pieces were painted, cut out and mounted, and how the hologram was made to turn.
- [making-of/prompts.md](https://cockpit-ui.vercel.app/making-of/prompts.md): every image and video prompt and setting, in order.
